HandoffResident.description:
One resident's line of the shift handoff (SPEC section 9).

`flags` counts the sessions inside the window that scored above this resident's
own threshold, which is the evidence a flag rests on rather than the flag itself:
one bad session never alerts (SPEC section 7). `pending_review` counts the alerts
raised for them that nobody has given a verdict on yet. `previous_flags` is the
same count for the window before this one, so a nurse coming on shift can read
whether this resident is getting better or worse rather than only a number.

`previous_flags` defaults to 0 for the same reason `monitoring_paused` does: it
was added after the payload shipped, so an older or trimmed handoff still
validates (T292, T311) and a dashboard reading it knows "no comparison sent"
from "none last shift".

room.description: The resident's room, so a handed-over line says where to go (SPEC section 9) and the printed or pasted handoff is usable on its own.
room.title: Room

flags.description: Sessions in the window above this resident's bar.
flags.title: Flags

previous_flags.description: The same count for the window just before this one (`[now - 2 x hours, now - hours)`), measured against the same bar, so a row can say more, fewer or the same as last shift. A count, never a verdict.
previous_flags.title: Previous Flags

pending_review.description: Alerts in the window with no verdict yet.
pending_review.title: Pending Review

trending.description: Their error score is on a slow rise. Read over their whole history, not this window: a drift takes weeks to show (SPEC section 7.5).
trending.title: Trending

monitoring_paused.description: Their room's monitoring is paused (SPEC section 12), so a quiet row means nobody was looking rather than nothing happened.
monitoring_paused.title: Monitoring Paused

description:
The shift handoff (`GET /handoff`, SPEC section 9).

What the nurse coming on shift missed: one row per resident for the window,
rows worth a look first, quiet ones listed too so the unit is visibly looked at
rather than silently skipped. `paused` is every room nobody was watching.
